finalists.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
finalists.why: The presence of a positive beta2-glycoprotein IgA antiphospholipid antibody and a new macular rash on the patient's chest that extended to his arms, along with rising serum creatinine, strongly support this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
finalists.why: The combination of fevers, joint pains, confusion, and significantly elevated liver enzymes (AST 1461 U/L and ALT 812 U/L) without a clear alternative explanation makes this a strong candidate.

frontier_selector.why: The decisive evidence of a positive beta2-glycoprotein IgA antiphospholipid antibody in the context of the patient's clinical presentation, including renal infarcts and a new macular rash, tips the balance in favor of Antiphospholipid syndrome.
